searchText: We found an unfixed corner-case, deposits: https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/a0619b279aa57140768859767be392ff5a20f656/packages/types/src/gloas/sszTypes.ts#L242 and don't we have a similar issue in beacon block body? in GLOAS, "deposits" must be 0 but it is enforced only at gossip\stf Yeah, the linked line from lodestar is exactly the deposits deserialization but checked late leading to memory amp from blocks under max payload size with a large number of deposits (~8k) we can probably limit that to 0 in the container, but generally, can't you do the same with deposit requests, since those are unbounded? Yes, I think so. The deserialization DoS primitive is not limited to beacon block gossip with non-canonical deposits but I don't think we can limit the deposits requests anymore, so the limit there is the max gossip limit The spec leaves out deposit requests check: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/gloas/p2p-interface.md#new-verify_execution_requests_limits Aha, understood. They are intentionally left out in CL specs because they are gas bound in the EL 🙏 I can confirm that even with Teku's conservative 10 message byte-cap for unknown parent block roots, lots of beacon block gossip with about 50k deposit requests each can DoS a teku node with 32GB RAM and 8GB heap limits. Requires about 500 beacon block gossip messages. The byte-cap helps but the issue is in deserialization. Sig check does not help because it happens too late yeah.. i have an alternative version of that PR that applies the limits deeper in the ssz, close to each field. But with such approach reference tests need big changes. Let's talk about these stuff later in ACDT <@504202741933932544> regarding the spec test harness, we added this handler ```ts // Only an ssz list limit violation is an expected input error, anything else is a decode bug shouldErrorOnInput: (error: Error, inputNames: Set<string>) =>!inputNames.has("post") && /over limit/.test(error.message) ``` so the `inputNames.has("post")` is what Justin mentioned, and we have a specific error message in our ssz lib so you have a map ( test -> expectedError ) for each of those tests?

excerpts.author: bshastry
excerpts.content: We found an unfixed corner-case, deposits: https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/a0619b279aa57140768859767be392ff5a20f656/packages/types/src/gloas/sszTypes.ts#L242

excerpts.author: tbenr
excerpts.content: and don't we have a similar issue in beacon block body? in GLOAS, "deposits" must be 0 but it is enforced only at gossip\stf

excerpts.author: bshastry
excerpts.content: Yeah, the linked line from lodestar is exactly the deposits deserialization but checked late leading to memory amp from blocks under max payload size with a large number of deposits (~8k)

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: we can probably limit that to 0 in the container, but generally, can't you do the same with deposit requests, since those are unbounded?

excerpts.author: bshastry
excerpts.content: Yes, I think so. The deserialization DoS primitive is not limited to beacon block gossip with non-canonical deposits

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: but I don't think we can limit the deposits requests anymore, so the limit there is the max gossip limit

excerpts.author: bshastry
excerpts.content: The spec leaves out deposit requests check: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/gloas/p2p-interface.md#new-verify_execution_requests_limits

excerpts.author: bshastry
excerpts.content: Aha, understood. They are intentionally left out in CL specs because they are gas bound in the EL 🙏

excerpts.author: bshastry
excerpts.content: I can confirm that even with Teku's conservative 10 message byte-cap for unknown parent block roots, lots of beacon block gossip with about 50k deposit requests each can DoS a teku node with 32GB RAM and 8GB heap limits. Requires about 500 beacon block gossip messages. The byte-cap helps but the issue is in deserialization. Sig check does not help because it happens too late

excerpts.author: tbenr
excerpts.content: yeah.. i have an alternative version of that PR that applies the limits deeper in the ssz, close to each field. But with such approach reference tests need big changes. Let's talk about these stuff later in ACDT

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content:
<@504202741933932544> regarding the spec test harness, we added this handler
```ts
// Only an ssz list limit violation is an expected input error, anything else is a decode bug
shouldErrorOnInput: (error: Error, inputNames: Set<string>) =>!inputNames.has("post") && /over limit/.test(error.message)
```
so the `inputNames.has("post")` is what Justin mentioned, and we have a specific error message in our ssz lib
